preamble: The offglide of /au/ hardens into the labiodental fricative [v], leaving the sequence [av]. In Greek this happened through /aw/ > [aβ] > /av/ by the late Koine period, with [av] before vowels and voiced consonants and [af] before voiceless ones. Comparable glide fortition independently produced [av] from earlier [aw] in Armenian (where աւ became [av] before vowels and word-finally but [o] before consonants) and in Modern Hebrew, where the old /w/ of waw merged with [β] into /v/.

examples.note: Before the voiced consonant /l/ the fricative is voiced.
Word-final աւ gives [ɑv] in both Eastern and Western Armenian; before consonants աւ instead became [o] (Old Armenian աւր 'day' > օր [or]).
Word-final -āw became [av] when historical /w/ merged with fricative [β] into /v/.
